To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TAC3 gene product NKB is a key regulator of LH release, which has been conserved from fish (zebrafish) to mammals (humans).

(1) the KNDy neuron model for GnRH and LH regulation is conserved in zebrafis; (2) TAC3 genes are duplicated in fish and encode two tachykinins, NKB and the novel NKB-related peptide; (3) the two TAC2 genes in fish are not duplicated, and the TAC2 gene product, NPY, may be involved in the reproductive functions of zebrafish.

the reproductive functions and neuroanatomy of tachy-kinin system in fish are different from those in mammals, and that NKB-related peptide may be an important regulator of reproductive functions in fish.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the tachikinin system and its reproductive functions in fish, which is a model organism for studying the evolutionary origins of vertebrate neuroendocrine regulation.
the reproductive functions of the tachykinnin system, and its regulation and actions at the hypothalamic, pituitary and gonadal levels.
understanding the reproductive functions of the TAC3/kNDy system in fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KNDy neuron model is a good starting point but needs more evidence and modification to accommodate the emerging story in the TAC3 gene regulation of reproductive functions from fish to mammals.
the KNDy neuron model in mammals is not yet fully applicable to fish, and the TAC3/kNDy system in fish may be a unique system with its own evolutionary story.
NKB is a key regulator of reproductive functions, and its actions in the brain are likely conserved from fish (and possibly other vertebrates) to mammals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NKB is a key peptide for the reproductive functions in both mammals and fish.
the "KNDys" are not only the master regulators of GnRH pulsatility and LH release in mammals and fish but also the key players for the reproductive functions of the gonad and the placenta.
NKB, a member of the tachikinin family, is an essential peptide for reproductive functions, and the KNDy neuron model is an excellent example of "neuroendocrinology of the 21st century".
The main takeaway from our work is that
NKB and its receptor NK3R play a key role in regulating reproductive functions in mammals and zebrafish.

the reproductive functions for NKB are conserved from fish (zebrafish) to mammals (humans), but the underlying mechanisms for NKB action may have evolved to adapt to different physiological and reproductive needs in different vertebrate species.
the KNDy neuron model may be a useful concept for studying the neuroendocrine control of reproduction across the vertebrate species, including teleost fish.
